body: The sun had barely cleared the rooftops when the market opened. Stalls of bread, fruit and flowers lined the narrow street, and the smell of coffee drifted between them. Nobody was in a hurry yet.

The old clock in the hall had never worked properly. It ran fast in summer and stopped completely in winter. Nobody fixed it, because after fifty years the wrong time had become the right one.

Rain arrived late that afternoon and stayed for three days. The streets turned to rivers, the gutters filled with leaves, and the whole city learned again how slowly water moves when it has nowhere to go.
